thread.title: Thomas Massie raises concerns over national debt and meat industry regulation
thread.title_full: Thomas Massie raises concerns over national debt and meat industry regulation

author: M. S. Herrick
title: Thomas Massie raises concerns over national debt and meat industry regulation
text:
U.S. Congressman Thomas Massie, representing Kentucky’s 4th district, posted a series of statements on social media addressing the national debt and the state of meat labeling and market control in the United States.
On October 21, 2025, Massie commented on the accuracy of his self-built debt badge in tracking the U.S. national debt. He wrote, “The debt badge I built calibrates to the penny with https://t.co/DT79kIMjzy, but the last time they published the debt was on 10/17, so it projects that debt to today’s debt based on the debt per second over the last year. By my calculations, the debt just crossed $38 trillion! https://t.co/bJ2qcdukOr”.
Later that day, Massie addressed meat labeling regulations, specifically concerning beef and pork imports. He asked, “When beef & pork are imported into the U.S., should companies be required to label the country of origin? Cars, tools, clothes, phones, and even chicken and seafood have country of origin labels. In 2015 Congress removed the beef & pork labels even though I voted to keep them.”
The following morning, Massie discussed market concentration in the meat industry. He stated, “Four corporations control 85% of meat sold in the U.S. Two are owned by China & Brazil. Farmers are being squeezed and consumers are being gouged. The answer is NOT to flood the market with foreign meat. We can solve this by passing my PRIME Act. Watch:https://t.co/OGTJ22GvWF”.
Massie has represented Kentucky’s 4th congressional district since 2012 after replacing Geoff Davis and previously served in local government roles in Kentucky. Born in Huntington, West Virginia in 1971, Massie is 52 years old and resides in Garrison. He holds a Bachelor of Science degree from Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT), graduating in 1993.
